headers.//: HTML entry points must NEVER cache. They reference the JS bundle by a hashed filename; if the HTML is cached the browser keeps loading an old bundle hash even after a redeploy. This is what was making the latest test deploys appear to do nothing on mobile.

Hashed static assets (Expo emits filenames like entry-<32-char-hash>.js for every build) are safe to cache forever — any code change rotates the filename, so a cached old version can never be served against new HTML.
Manifest, icons, fonts — change rarely but should pick up within a day when they do.
